blocks.text: David’s capture of the stronghold, his settlement there, and the construction of his house mark Jerusalem as the royal center of his kingdom. The narrative’s next movement brings the ark to this city, but only after an earlier attempt at transporting it ends with Uzzah’s death. This sequence keeps the establishment of David’s rule and the ark’s arrival distinct while placing both developments in Jerusalem.

Archaeology supports the existence of a later Davidic dynasty, but it does not establish one uncontested picture of David’s kingdom—its size, administration, and chronology remain disputed. That caution matters when readers move from this narrative of royal consolidation to historical reconstruction.

This chapter belongs to a larger movement in 2 Samuel: David’s accession and consolidation of rule are followed by the ark’s arrival and the dynasty promise, then by royal abuse, violence within David’s household, rebellion, grief, and a closing appendix. The broader shape prevents the early account of growing strength from being read as the whole of David’s story.
